statuses.Delivered: Done as committed, shown by an official record (a law, a council decision, a completed project).
statuses.Delivered late: Done, but after the date that was committed.
statuses.On track: Under way and, on the evidence, meeting its committed timeline or targets.
statuses.In progress: Under way; too early to say whether it will be on time.
statuses.Partly delivered: Some of the commitment is done and some is not.
statuses.Stalled: Started, but no measurable progress for a long time, or put on hold.
statuses.Broken: Abandoned, reversed or ruled out by the person or government who made it.
statuses.Not yet assessed: Listed, but the evidence is not yet strong enough to rate it.

commitments.who: Mayor Jeromy Farkas; Coun. Andre Chabot (Ward 10) brought the motion
commitments.title: Repeal citywide ("blanket") rezoning
commitments.progress: Council approved the repeal on April 8, 2026 (first reading 12 to 3). Properties return to their pre-2024 zoning on August 4, 2026, and each change of land use goes back to a public hearing.

evidence.text: Council approves repeal of citywide rezoning
Council decision summary and project page

history.note: Said after the election that he would work with council to repeal the bylaw (reported by CBC, quoted by LiveWire Calgary).

commitments.title: Replace citywide rezoning with a targeted, community-informed approach that builds homes faster and more affordably
commitments.progress: Changes to the rowhouse (R-CG) rules were sent back for more testing in April 2026. No replacement housing plan had been adopted as of the last check.

evidence.text: R-CG amendment sent back for testing

commitments.disputed: An opinion piece by More Neighbours Calgary (March 3, 2026) argues the plan has not been delivered; shown as in progress because no replacement plan has been adopted yet.

commitments.who: City of Calgary, with the Government of Canada (Housing Accelerator Fund)
commitments.title: About 6,800 more homes than Calgary's usual pace, over three years, with $228 million from the federal Housing Accelerator Fund
commitments.progress: By February 28, 2025, 34,594 of 41,858 units counted toward the agreement were permitted (83% of the target in the first year). Canada added $22.8 million in March 2025 for exceeding targets; non-market units were the furthest behind (186 of 740).

evidence.text: City receives additional funding for exceeding housing targets

history.note: 83% of the unit target reached in year one; bonus funding.

commitments.title: Replace the Bearspaw South feeder main, the water main that broke in 2024, by the end of 2026
commitments.progress: On June 15, 2026 all five segments were under construction and the City said the project was more than halfway done (stage A tunnelling 51% complete). The City warns weather, new breaks or missing inspection data could delay it.

evidence.text: Construction set to finish by the end of 2026

commitments.who: City of Calgary, Government of Alberta and Calgary Sports and Entertainment Corporation
commitments.title: Build Scotia Place, the new event centre, to open for the 2027 NHL season, on budget
commitments.progress: The City reported the project on time and on budget (December 2025, updated January 2026). The steel ring around the main bowl was connected in June 2026; the aim is to seal the building by the end of 2026.

funding.promised: City $515 million upfront; CSEC $40 million upfront plus $17 million a year for 35 years; Province: infrastructure around the site

commitments.who: City of Calgary, Government of Alberta and Government of Canada
commitments.title: Build the first phase of the Green Line LRT in southeast Calgary
commitments.progress: Council voted to wind the project down on September 17, 2024; a month later the City and Province agreed to build the southeast section. Groundbreaking for phase 1 was June 26, 2025. Stage 1 is costed at $5.5 billion, shared about equally by the three governments.

evidence.source: Wikipedia (summary of City and news sources)

funding.promised: About one third each from the City, Alberta and Canada

history.note: City and Province agree on the southeast section.

commitments.who: United Conservative Party; Premier Danielle Smith
commitments.title: Cut personal income tax with a new 8% bracket on the first $60,000 of income
commitments.progress: Delayed in Budget 2024 (February 2024); delivered in Budget 2025, saving about $750 a year for a single person and about $1,500 for a family, at about $1.2 billion a year.

evidence.text: Province stalls income tax break promised by Smith

commitments.who: Government of Alberta; Premier Danielle Smith
commitments.title: Put questions on Alberta's future, including whether to begin a separation process, to a province-wide referendum in 2026
commitments.progress: Held on October 19, 2026 with ten questions; province-wide turnout 67.0%. 82.4% of Calgary voters and 75.0% of Albertans chose for Alberta to remain a province (Question 10).

evidence.source: Election Data Centre on this website

commitments.who: Liberal Party of Canada; Government of Canada
commitments.title: Cut the lowest federal income tax rate from 15% to 14%
commitments.progress: Bill C-4 set the rate at 14.5% for 2025 and 14% from 2026, and received Royal Assent in March 2026.

evidence.text: Legislation to make life more affordable receives Royal Assent

commitments.who: Liberal Party of Canada; Government of Canada
commitments.title: Remove the GST for first-time buyers of new homes
commitments.progress: Bill C-4 created a temporary GST new-housing rebate for first-time home buyers; Royal Assent March 2026.

commitments.who: Liberal Party of Canada; Government of Canada
commitments.title: End the consumer carbon price
commitments.progress: Bill C-4 repeals the fuel charge (the consumer carbon price); the industrial carbon price stays.
